segmentChecks.note: The given/then/prefer/avoid fields retain entrypoint-based reachability, per-interlocking route_id uniqueness, and exactly-once continuation-or-terminal accounting.

Both continuation and terminal declarations on unreachable source interlockings are explicitly prohibited.
Continuation cycles are rejected, including intended loops, until an explicit bounded/intentional loop construct exists.
The why field preserves bilateral binding's single-routing-decision scope, while avoid retains the implicit code-only handoff concern.
The why field concisely retains explicit journey topology and all four named failure modes.

risks: The closure walk has no explicit visited-set or traversal algorithm, so a weak implementation could naively recurse forever on a cyclic graph instead of reporting the cycle; the required rejection itself is nevertheless unambiguous.
